statement: Metals form positive ions.
An anion is a positive ion.
explanation: An anion is negative; a cation is positive.

statement: Acids have a pH below 7.
The nucleus contains protons and electrons.
explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons.

statement: A neutron has no charge.
For Groups I to VII, the number of outer-shell electrons is the same as the group number.
The number of occupied electron shells is the same as the period number.
A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons.
Alkalis turn red litmus blue.
An acid and a carbonate react to give a salt and hydrogen.
explanation: They give a salt, water and carbon dioxide.

statement: Group I metals become less reactive down the group.
explanation: They become more reactive down the group.

statement: Bromine is a red-brown liquid at room temperature.
The halogens are diatomic: chlorine gas is Cl₂.
The noble gases are monatomic.
Elements in the same period have similar chemical properties.
explanation: Elements in the same group have similar properties.

statement: Isotopes of an element have different numbers of protons.
explanation: Isotopes have the same number of protons and different numbers of neutrons.

statement: Solid ionic compounds conduct electricity well.
explanation: They conduct only when molten or dissolved, when the ions can move.

statement: Thymolphthalein is colourless in acid and blue in alkali.
Methyl orange is yellow in acid.
explanation: Methyl orange is red in acid and yellow in alkali.

statement: In a word equation, the products are written on the left.
explanation: The reactants go on the left and the products on the right.

statement: Group II metals form ions with a 2+ charge.
The relative charge of an electron is −1.
The relative mass of an electron is 1.
explanation: It is almost nothing (about 1/1840); protons and neutrons have a relative mass of 1.

statement: A strong acid is completely dissociated in water.
Ethanoic acid is a strong acid.
explanation: Ethanoic acid is a weak acid: it is only partly dissociated.

statement: Oxygen is a metal.
Water is a compound.
Sodium is in Group I.
Acids have a pH above 7.
explanation: Acids have a pH below 7; alkalis are above 7.
